facts: The appellants, who were accused 1 to 3 in the trial before the Additional Sessions Judge, Satara, were charged u/s. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for the offence of internationally causing the death of one Malhari (hereinafter referred to as the deceased) and S. 324 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for the offence of voluntarily causing hurt to one Babu Shaikh.

The charge was sought to be substantiated by three categories of evidence: (1) evidence of Hiralal Sutar and Babu Shaikh, both of whom claimed to be eyewitnesses to the incident resulting in the death of the deceased and injuries to Babu Shaikh, (2) evidence of dying declarations made by the deceased before Dinkar Kunte and police Patil Madhavrao Dhayagude and (3) evidence of recovery of bloodstained clothes from accused 1, 2 and 3.
The learned Additional Sessions Judge was not satisfied with this evidence and taking the view that it suffered from considerable discrepancies and improbabilities, he acquitted all the accused.
issues: Whether the High Court was correct in setting aside the acquittal of accused 1 and 3 and convicting them for the offence of intentionally causing the death of the deceased.
Whether the evidence of Hiralal Sutar is reliable and can be relied upon to prove the guilt of accused 1 and 3.
petitioner_arguments: The appellants argued that the High Court was in error in setting aside the acquittal of accused 1 and 3 and convicting them for the offence of intentionally causing the death of the deceased.
They also argued that the evidence of Hiralal Sutar is unreliable and cannot be relied upon to prove the guilt of accused 1 and 3.
respondent_arguments: The respondent argued that the High Court was correct in setting aside the acquittal of accused 1 and 3 and convicting them for the offence of intentionally causing the death of the deceased.
They also argued that the evidence of Hiralal Sutar is reliable and can be relied upon to prove the guilt of accused 1 and 3.
court_reasoning: The court held that the High Court was correct in setting aside the acquittal of accused 1 and 3 and convicting them for the offence of intentionally causing the death of the deceased.
It also held that the evidence of Hiralal Sutar is reliable and can be relied upon to prove the guilt of accused 1 and 3.
holding: The court convicted accused 1, 2 and 3 for the offence of intentionally causing the death of the deceased and sentenced each of them to suffer imprisonment for life.
It also convicted accused 3 for the offence of voluntarily causing hurt to Babu Shaikh and sentenced him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year.
